title: Sequoia Analytics — inference integration jot
content:
Context / who: Quick personal capture after kickoff with Sequoia Analytics (lead: Priyanka Reddy, eng lead: Tomas Ortega). They build domain-specific forecasting assistants for CPG clients. Want private deployment (VPC) with PII data in prompts; timeline: POC in 6 weeks, production in ~Q3.

High-level asks from call:
- Private deployment (VPC peering) + optional on-prem connector for sensitive datasets.
- Low-latency query path for interactive analyst UI (95th p99 target under 120ms for short prompts).
- Batch/async scoring for nightly runs (throughput ~3k requests/minute at 128 tokens average).
- Cost target: they want to keep hosted cost ~<= $0.002/token equivalent — implies quantized model / batching / prefix caching.
- Strong audit logging and key management (KMS integration required).

Immediate impressions / gotchas to flag:
1) Tokenization mismatch risk
- They use a homegrown preprocessor (domain-normalization: SKU codes, weird delimiters). We must check that client-side tokenization matches the model tokenizer (esp. if they want to do embeddings + generation hybrid). TODO: get sample dataset (10k lines) and run tokenization locally vs model to estimate token inflation.
- Action: ask Tomas for representative text and the preprocess script. Add to JIRA-CA-4721.

2) KV-cache warmup / cold-start for interactive UI
- Their analyst UI tends to do many short-turn multi-shot prompts where context shares long product descriptions. If we use prefix caching we can save tokens; but warmup latency on first query per user could blow p99. Need to tune TTL on cache and pre-warm common prefixes on session creation.
- Note: Dedicated pools vs hosted fallback: if they use Dedicated we can pin model to reduce cold-start jitter. If Private (VPC) we still need a small warm pool.
- Action: propose pre-warm strategy in POC design doc.

3) Quantization and output quality trade-offs
- They are cost sensitive. We should run evals comparing fp16 -> 4/8-bit quant profiles on their exact prompt set (esp. SKU hallucination edge cases). Some quant configs degrade numeric precision (important for forecast reasoning).
- Plan: run Redwood Optimize recommended quant profile matrix for their workload; capture quality drop in key metrics.

4) Network topology + egress & VPC peering
- They require VPC peering with an isolated subnet. Need to clarify whether they want: (A) Private control plane + customer-managed runtime in their VPC, or (B) Redwood-managed runtime with VPC egress restrictions.
- Important for logging: if logs must remain in their cloud account, we need to wire log sink (S3/GCS) and IAM roles.
- Action: capture network diagram from their infra team. Add ticket for infra to map peering steps (confl link).

5) Rate limits / burst capacity expectations
- Nightly batch runs may cause a large delta in capacity needs. They want near-zero queueing for real-time UI but can accept throttling for batch jobs. We should recommend separate routes/keys with different policies: interactive route (low latency, high priority) vs batch route (cheap, throughput oriented).
- Also discuss autoscaling cooldowns — they have predictable batch window at 02:00 local time. Consider reserved bursts for that window.

6) Privacy / prompt provenance
- Must record prompt source with minimal token overhead. They asked for redaction helpers: suggestion is to keep raw prompts in their account (log sink) and only ship hashed/annotated prompt id to Redwood logs.
- KMS: they will use AWS KMS — confirm algorithm (RSA vs KMS envelope) and rotation policy.

7) Eval and regression detection
- They rely on numerically precise outputs (e.g., convert SKU strings to codes, generate CSV-like outputs). Need guardrails: structured output schema + strict parsers. Add auto-regression tests in Redwood Optimize using their golden prompt set.

Open questions to resolve (need answers before architecture design)
- Do they want a single model for both embeddings and generation? (They lean toward separate optimized models but want a simple API.)
- Expected median sequence length for interactive flows (they said "usually under 150 tokens" but need distribution). Request histogram.
- Which cloud region(s) do they expect traffic from? Mostly us-west-2 and eu-west-1.
- SLA expectations for Private tier — they asked for 99.9% uptime, clarify acceptable maintenance windows.

POC plan (6 weeks) — rough milestones
- Week 0–1: infra discovery + tokenization sample ingestion + network diagram (deliverable: infra checklist)
- Week 2: baseline quality eval (fp16 baseline) vs two quant profiles on their prompt sets (deliverable: QC matrix)
- Week 3–4: deploy POC Private control plane in customer dev VPC, integrate log sink + KMS (deliverable: test deployment + smoke tests)
- Week 5: integrate interactive UI route with prefix caching + pre-warm; measure p95/p99 latency
- Week 6: run batch window simulation, cost projection, handoff doc

Immediate next steps (today / this week)
- Send follow-up email with itemized ask list + request sample data (Maya to send by 2026-03-13).
- Schedule 45min infra call with Tomas + their network/security (target 2026-03-15). Ravi to own.
- Create JIRA epic CA-4721 and tasks for: tokenization check, quant eval, VPC peering checklist, logging/KMS integration, caching strategy doc.
- Prep small benchmark harness: start with 500 representative prompts -> run fp16 & q4_0 & q2_0 (or nearest quant profiles) to get ROUGE/precision on numeric fields.

Notes to self / talking points for infra call
- Confirm whether they can accept Private control plane in Redwood account but using VPC peering vs fully customer-run runtime.
- If we ask them to host runtime, we need clear operator-level access requirements and support SLAs (ops runbook to be drafted).
- Bring up warm-pool sizing: for interactive, recommend minimum 3 GPUs reserved per region for their team during core hours.

Loose ideas (exploratory)
- Consider a hybrid pricing model: reserved baseline capacity for interactive + usage for batch bursts (gives them cost predictability).
- Offer to template prompt redaction library in their codebase to keep Redwood logs minimal.

End notes: This doc is messy — convert to a tidy handoff doc and POC scoping brief once we have sample prompts and network diagram. Keep CA-4721 updated.
